prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: reference target plate for natural procedural trees. Produce a high resolution 4 by 3 botanical photographic contact sheet with twelve labelled tree architecture families on neutral grey, natural diffuse daylight, each panel a whole small tree and detailed leafy branch inset. 1 Oak and beech: alternating broad leaves with variable pitch, uneven lobes, branches of different ages. 2 Maple and sweetgum: maple opposite decussate pairs, sweetgum alternating star leaves, no identical silhouettes. 3 Birch and cherry: alternating serrated leaves on long and short shoots. 4 Willow and eucalyptus: long pendent leaves, individually varied curvature and pitch, tapering shoots. 5 Ginkgo: fan blades in irregular short shoot clusters plus long shoots. 6 Pines: needles in fascicles on age-related cohorts and irregular branch whorls. 7 Dawn redwood and deciduous conifers: opposite soft flat foliage on gently curved branchlets, varied branchlet rolls. 8 Olive and evergreen laurels: opposite olive narrow leathery leaves, alternate laurel broad leaves, variable exposure and orientation. 9 Acacias and jacaranda: fine bipinnate leaves, pinnae and leaflets individually tilted around the rachis, green feathery volumes not flat identical stamps. 10 Baobab and palmate tropical trees: compound blades with separate leaflet attitudes on age-varied shoots, thick trunk. 11 Marula, ash and sausage tree: pinnate compound leaves with asymmetric leaflet size and rotation, curved rachises. 12 Tropical broadleaf, fig and yellowwood: layered branch frameworks, young flushes smaller, leaves individually rolled and bent, twig tips always ending in buds or live growth. Each plant must have irregular but anatomically constrained branch/leaf distribution, no repeated copied geometry, preserve opposite pairs and alternate attachment, no floating leaves, no extreme crumpling, avoid generic round green blobs. Reference images for code refinement, botanical anatomy has priority over decorative symmetry.
